text:
mike: Heads-up: hit a weird loop in the python sample app when token rotation and client leases are enabled. Pages replayed, downstream got 429s.

ana: Can you share a short repro/logs?

mike: gist: token refresh triggers lease release -> other workers pick same cursor -> duplicate fetch -> retries -> 429 flood. Logs: `leases: released 3`, `paginator: cursor=abc123`, `fetch: 429`.

sophia: Sounds like race on cursor ownership. Sample app persists cursor in-memory only, so multiple processes can claim it.

ana: Also noticed lease_ttl was 1.5s in that test, token rotate ~300ms. Very small ttl increases contention.

infra-ops: Quick mitigation: SDK should avoid immediate lease release on auth swap. Suggest stall window 400-1200ms with jitter. Also add an idempotency header per page request.

mike: Proposed plan: (1) SDK change: on auth change mark leases stalled for jitter window; (2) SDK helper idempotency_key_for_cursor(cursor); (3) sample app: persist cursor with CAS using sqlite/redis.

sophia: I'll add sampleapp fix and a flag to disable aggressive lease release.

ana: I'll prototype SDK unit + integration tests simulating token churn.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: branch=devex/lease-auth-fix reviewers=@ana,@sophia. CI pending.

mike: Also add onboarding note: "if you use token refresh + leases, persist cursor and set lease_ttl >= 3s".

infra-ops: Add metric `dup_page.per_min` and alert >5/min.

mike: assigning tasks in GH after lunch.
